score_evidence.D: Hard parts get worked examples: the attempt-count table (L430), the backoff table (L741), the steering counter table (L655), the compression ratio (L351). Easy facts are repeated, for example tool failure returns an error result (L77, L81, L175, L369, L874).
score_evidence.E: Good comparison tables (error routing L85, writable fields L162, stop reasons L892, cancel checkpoints L910, retry means L866) and ASCII flow diagrams. The formula at L425 adds little. No figures (only ASCII).
score_evidence.F: All 15 sampled claims are supported. Wrong statements outside the sample: (1) L729 '검증을 통과한 RefundDecision은 result.structured_output에 담깁니다': with the post's Cedar policy, the structured-output tool 'RefundDecision' is denied ('DENIED: Access denied by Cedar policy'), so the call ends limit_structured_output_attempts with no output (reproduced). (2) L509 'handle_refund는 바꿀 필요가 없습니다': OrderToolAuth's allow-list {lookup_order, send_email} denies 'RefundDecision' ('DENIED: Tool RefundDecision is not allowed'), so handle_refund always returns None (reproduced). (3) The L685 recap describes build_agent() contents that do not exist. (4) The model id 'global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-20260301-v1:0' (L117 and others) appears in no fetched docs page (unverified).
score_evidence.T1: A lot of real code with correct kwargs (limits, cancel_signal, invocation_state, interruptResponse). But there is no install command anywhere (and Cedar needs the strands-agents[cedar] extra). OrderIdSteering lacks the required 'name' and raises TypeError, so every agent built after L645 fails. The structured-output decision is blocked by the post's own authorization layers.
score_evidence.T2: Covers the topics the sources support (agent loop, hooks, middleware, conversation management, structured output, interventions, steering, HITL/Cedar, retries, lifecycle controls) in a sensible order, and flags inconsistencies between docs pages (max_delay 128 vs 240 at L752, middleware removal at L301, the Deny escalation contradiction at L493).
score_evidence.T3: Explains internals and why they are designed that way: hook order and reversed After callbacks (L154-156), hooks outside the middleware chain (L305), best-effort proactive compression (L353), the schema-as-tool design (L365), the decision-precedence rationale (L467), retry nesting with middleware (L864), deployment shapes and OTEL (L1047-1084), failure modes (L1105). The trade-offs read as recommendations.
